summary: Settlement processing stalled at ~07:42Z because order-service v2.16.0 (deployed 07:40Z, the only deploy in the window) renamed the OrderExecuted field qty->quantity and added a v2 schema header, while settlement-service's consumer still expects schema v1; the first v2 message at orders-3@8841207 fails deserialization ('missing required field qty', header v2) and is retried forever, blocking that partition and freezing all settlement progress (confidence 0.72, medium). The onset is tightly aligned: deploy 07:40:00, lag rise 07:37-07:44, throughput collapse 07:42:00, first bad log 07:42:14. Alternatives were rejected on mechanical grounds rather than mere absence of evidence: the reporter's cfg-3004 poll change cannot block an offset (the consumer is actively polling and retrying), the shared ledger-db is healthy (flat db_pool_in_use and 5xx), and a broker-wide event is contradicted by the healthy sibling consumer notification-service on the same shared broker (flat lag ~60, normal throughput, zero under-replication). The remaining weakness is that no per-partition or producer-side telemetry directly proves offset 8841207 was emitted by order-service, and no rollback/restart was attempted to serve as a natural experiment.

ranked_hypotheses.title: order-service v2.16.0 schema rename (qty->quantity, header v2) produces a poison message that blocks partition orders-3
ranked_hypotheses.statement: order-service v2.16.0 (deployed 07:40) changed the OrderExecuted event schema: field qty renamed to quantity and a v2 schema header added. settlement-service's consumer (built for schema v1) cannot deserialize the first v2 message at orders-3@8841207, throws 'missing required field qty', and retries that offset indefinitely, blocking the partition. No offsets advance, so lag grows monotonically and zero settlements post.

causal_chain.claim: order-service v2.16.0 deploys at 07:40:00Z, the single deployment in the fleet window, renaming OrderExecuted field qty->quantity, adding field venue, and adding a v2 schema version header; status live, not rolled back
order-service is a declared producer ('queue-produce') to the shared kafka broker that settlement-service consumes, so it is a legitimate writer to the orders topic

settlement-service's consumer expects schema v1 and cannot deserialize the v2 message: 'failed to deserialize OrderExecuted at orders-3@8841207: missing required field qty (schema v1 expected, header says v2)'
The error header version (v2) and the missing field name (qty) match order-service v2.16.0's declared changes exactly, linking the poison message content to that release
The single poison message at orders-3@8841207 blocks the partition and is retried without advancing the offset ('poison message: retrying orders-3@8841207, partition blocked')
No offsets advance, so settlement throughput collapses (~65 -> ~0.4 req/s) and consumer lag grows monotonically (~50 -> 60k+)

assumptions: The v2 message at orders-3@8841207 was produced by order-service specifically (no per-partition producer telemetry exists; linkage rests on deploy-content + error-text match + timing)
settlement-service's consumer was not updated in lockstep with the v2 schema (no settlement-service deployment in window per F1/F35)
The poll-config change cfg-3004 is coincidental/ineffective as a stall cause (no poll/rebalance/timeout log evidence, F11)
The poison message blocks partition orders-3 only; errors on other partitions of the orders topic are not visible in the retrieved (truncated) logs

ranked_hypotheses.title: Broker-side partition reassignment / infra event on the shared kafka broker caused the stall (historical analogy)
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A broker-side disruption (partition reassignment, rebalance, broker maintenance) on the shared kafka broker stalled the settlement consumer, matching HIST-112/HIST-104. The poison message and v2 deploy are incidental.

causal_chain.claim: A broker-side reassignment/rebalance occurs on the shared kafka broker (unrecorded; no broker rebalance/reassignment metric exists to observe it)
settlement-service loses/regains partition assignment and stops advancing offsets

assumptions: An unrecorded broker event occurred despite no kafka config change and no under-replication activity
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Rejected on direct sibling-consumer evidence, not merely absence of broker telemetry. The broker is shared by TWO consumers (F3, F25), yet the other consumer notification-service shows flat baseline lag (mean ~60, no rise at 07:42 or later — F20), fully normal flat throughput (132-167 req/s — F21), and no rebalance/session-timeout/poll-timeout logs (only one unrelated NTP message — F22). under_replicated_partitions is exactly 0.0 for every bucket (F23). A broker-wide reassignment affecting the shared broker would degrade both consumers; the impact is confined to settlement-service, and the observed error is a content-specific deserialization failure at a named offset (F10), not an assignment loss. Historical analogy (HIST-112/104) carries no dependency/partition telemetry (F14/F15) and no poison-message precedent exists in the corpus (F16).

ranked_hypotheses.title: settlement-service cfg-3004 poll-settings change caused the consumer to stop fetching (reporter's suspicion)
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The settlement-service config change cfg-3004 at 07:35 (consumer.max.poll.records 500->200) triggered the stall — e.g. a mis-set poll parameter caused the consumer to stop advancing. This is the reporter's stated suspicion.

causal_chain.claim: cfg-3004 changes consumer.max.poll.records 500->200 at 07:35, preceding the stall
Mis-set poll parameter causes consumer to stop fetching/deserializing, so no offsets advance

assumptions: max.poll.records=200 is small enough to throttle fetch to a full stall (implausible — 200 is a normal batch size)
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Mechanism mismatch: reducing max.poll.records to 200 slows batch size, it does not block an offset or stop all progress, and the consumer demonstrably IS polling and actively retrying offset 8841207 (F10/F28). No rebalance-loop, session-timeout, or poll-timeout logs exist — the only error signatures are the deserialization/poison patterns (F11). No precedent exists in the corpus for a max.poll.records-type setting causing a stall (F17). The actual failure is a content-specific deserialization error naming the v2 header and missing qty field (F10), which poll settings cannot produce.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Poison message from a source other than order-service's v2 schema blocks the partition
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A malformed/poison message (from a non-order-service source, or a pre-existing corrupt event) sits at orders-3@8841207 and blocks the partition, with order-service v2.16.0 merely coincident in time. settlement-service is victim, not cause.

causal_chain.claim: A malformed message is produced to orders-3 (source and timing unknown)
consumer cannot deserialize and retries offset 8841207 indefinitely, blocking the partition
Offsets stop advancing; throughput collapses and lag grows

assumptions: A malformed message could originate independently of the v2 schema change
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: The error text explicitly names the v2 schema: 'missing required field qty (schema v1 expected, header says v2)' (F10). The v2 header exactly matches order-service v2.16.0's added v2 schema version header, and 'qty' is exactly the field that release renamed to 'quantity' (F1/F32). This is the new schema, not random corruption; timing (deploy 07:40, first bad message 07:42:14) also aligns (F13).

ranked_hypotheses.title: Shared ledger-db degradation back-pressures settlement processing
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The shared ledger-db (used by four services) degraded, causing settlement-service's calls to hang and back-pressure the consumer, stalling settlements. Because the broker is shared, other services would surface it too.

causal_chain.claim: Shared ledger-db degrades (failover, IOPS throttling, disk full, slow scan — all precedented)
settlement-service DB calls slow/fail, holding the consumer
Throughput collapses and offsets stop advancing

assumptions: ledger-db degradation can stall the consumer at the message-deserialization stage (it cannot — deserialization is pre-DB)
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Mechanism mismatch: the failing action is message DESERIALIZATION, which occurs before any DB call can fail, so a DB fault cannot produce 'missing required field qty (schema v1 expected, header says v2)'. Metrics also contradict it: db_pool_in_use flat (~5.8-6.5) and HTTP 5xx error_rate flat (~0.17-0.26%) with no step change (F12), and no DB/ledger/posting/5xx error logs exist (F11). Only weak precedent (F18) supports it.

facts.statement: Exactly one deployment occurred across all services in 07:30-09:59: order-service v2.16.0 at 2026-05-12T07:40:00Z ('Order events v2'), which renames event field qty -> quantity, adds field venue, and adds event schema version header v2; status live, not rolled back.
Exactly one config change occurred in the window: settlement-service cfg-3004 at 07:35:00Z changing consumer.max.poll.records from 500 to 200.

The first bad log entry is at 07:42:14Z: deserialization failure 'failed to deserialize OrderExecuted at orders-3@8841207: missing required field 'qty' (schema v1 expected, header says v2)' (213 occurrences, first_seen 07:42:14) plus 'poison message: retrying orders-3@8841207 (attempt <n>), partition blocked' (196 occurrences, first_seen 07:44:51).

order-service's producer-side change content matches the consumer's poison-message signature exactly: dep-6010 lists 'OrderExecuted event: rename field qty -> quantity', 'add field venue', 'event schema version header v2' — the same missing field name and the same header version the consumer reports.
Settlement throughput collapsed from ~62-67 req/s to ~0.4 req/s between the 07:41 and 07:42 buckets and stayed at ~0.4 req/s through 09:55 (onset 07:42:00Z).

Consumer lag was flat/baseline (~36-56 messages) through 07:35, rose sharply from the 07:40-07:45 bucket (07:40 avg 515.03, 07:45 avg 2629.17), and grew monotonically to avg 60220.76 / max 61605.53 at 09:55.
The first error log (07:42:14Z) coincides with the first zero-throughput minute (07:42 bucket avg 0.39) and the lag rise in the 07:37-07:44 region, so all three signals onset together at ~07:42.

All 409 WARN+ entries in 07:30-09:59 are level ERROR and consist solely of the two orders-3 patterns; there are no rebalance-loop, session-timeout, poll-timeout, or DB/ledger/posting/5xx downstream-failure messages.

Every WARN+ log entry names ONLY partition orders-3 at offset 8841207; targeted searches for 'orders-0' and 'orders-1' returned 0 matches, and no other topic name appears in settlement-service logs. All 213 deserialization errors are at orders-3@8841207.
kafka is a shared broker with TWO consumers (settlement-service and notification-service), so a broker-wide disruption would affect both.

notification-service consumer lag is flat/baseline throughout 06:30-09:57 (mean ~60.11, no rise at 07:42 or later) and its throughput is normal and flat (min 132.42, max 166.73 req/s); its only WARN+ entry is an unrelated NTP clock-drift message at 08:39:18Z.
Broker metric under_replicated_partitions is exactly 0.0 for every 9-min bucket from 06:30 to 09:57 (no missing points).

Downstream/DB health indicators stayed flat across the stall: db_pool_in_use held ~5.8-6.5 connections (06:30-09:57) and HTTP 5xx error_rate stayed ~0.17-0.26% with no step change, arguing against a downstream call failure, connection-pool exhaustion, or ledger-db fault.

No rollback of order-service v2.16.0 occurred (dep-6010 is live, rolled_back_at null) and no settlement-service deployment/restart event exists in 07:30-09:59, so no event could have reset the blocked offset.
order-service has a produce edge to the shared kafka broker, making it a legitimate writer to the topic settlement-service consumes.
No historical incident in the searchable corpus matches today's poison-message/deserialization or producer-schema-rename signature, nor any case of a max.poll.records-type setting causing a stall.

assumptions: The v2 message at orders-3@8841207 was produced by order-service specifically. No per-partition or per-producer telemetry exists to link that offset to a producer (F26, F24); the linkage rests on deploy-content match (F32), the error text (F10), the produce edge from order-service to the shared broker (F36), and timing (F13).
settlement-service's consumer was not updated in lockstep with the v2 schema; the only deploy in the window is order-service v2.16.0 and there is no settlement-service deployment (F1, F35).

The cfg-3004 poll-settings change is coincidental/ineffective as a stall cause; there is no poll/rebalance/timeout log evidence and the consumer is actively polling and retrying the bad offset (F2, F10, F11).
The poison message blocks partition orders-3 only; the retrieved logs are truncated, so errors on other partitions of the orders topic may exist but are not visible (F27, F28, F31).

The retrieved log sample, though truncated, is assumed representative enough that no additional distinct error pattern (DB/posting/5xx) exists after 07:59; the pattern aggregate lists only the two orders-3 consumer-side patterns (F11, F31).

Historical precedent (HIST-112/HIST-104) is assumed non-diagnostic here: those broker/rebalance records carry no poison-message, partition, or offset telemetry and no producer-schema precedent exists in the corpus (F14, F15, F16, F19).

timeline.event: settlement-service config change cfg-3004: consumer.max.poll.records 500->200 by m.das (only config change in the window).
Aggregate consumer_lag begins rising from a flat ~47 avg (07:30 bucket) to 202.21 (07:37) and 2616.82 (07:44).
order-service v2.16.0 deployed ('Order events v2'): renames OrderExecuted field qty->quantity, adds venue, adds v2 schema header. Only deployment in the window; remains live.
Last normal settlement throughput bucket (avg ~65.3 req/s).
Settlement throughput collapses to ~0.4 req/s (07:42 bucket) and stays there through 09:55.
First deserialization error: 'failed to deserialize OrderExecuted at orders-3@8841207: missing required field 'qty' (schema v1 expected, header says v2)' — onset of the poison-message loop.
First 'poison message: retrying orders-3@8841207 (attempt n), partition blocked' log — the retry storm begins.
Incident INC-010 reported by on-call SRE: no settlements posted ~40 minutes, consumer lag 60k and climbing.
Only notification-service WARN+ entry in the window: unrelated NTP clock-drift resync message.
Lag plateaus at avg 60713.43 / max 61605.53; under_replicated_partitions still 0.0; db_pool_in_use and 5xx error_rate still flat.
Last deserialization error logged; partition orders-3 still blocked with no rollback or consumer restart applied.

recommended_actions.action: Roll back order-service to the pre-v2.16.0 producer contract (or set order-service to emit schema v1 / stop emitting the v2 header) so that new OrderExecuted events on orders-3 are again v1-compatible. This is the direct mitigation of the identified cause (the only deploy in-window, F1/F32/F33).
recommended_actions.rationale: The poison message is the v2-schema OrderExecuted event that settlement-service cannot deserialize (F10/F32); restoring v1 production stops new poison messages from being produced at the head of the partition.

recommended_actions.action: Unblock partition orders-3 for settlement-service: skip/quarantine the single poison record at orders-3@8841207 (e.g. via an offset-skip/seek-past-bad-record admin action or a dead-letter/poison-message handler), then verify offsets advance and lag declines.
recommended_actions.rationale: The consumer is stuck retrying the same offset indefinitely (213 deserialize errors, 196 blocked-retry entries, all at orders-3@8841207 — F10/F28/F29/F27); only clearing that record restores forward progress. No offset-skip/rollback mechanism is currently recorded (F34) and no restart has been applied (F35).

recommended_actions.action: Do NOT treat cfg-3004 (consumer.max.poll.records 500->200) as the cause and do not roll it back as the primary fix; keep it or revert at leisure. The consumer is demonstrably polling and actively retrying the bad offset, which a smaller batch size cannot produce.
recommended_actions.rationale: cfg-3004 is coincidental: the failure is a content-specific deserialization error naming the v2 header and missing qty field, a mechanism poll settings cannot produce (F10, F11, F17).

recommended_actions.action: Confirm recovery after offset skip / rollback: verify settlement throughput returns toward ~62-67 req/s and consumer_lag declines monotonically from ~60k, and confirm the settlement-service ERROR patterns (orders-3@8841207) cease.
recommended_actions.rationale: Recovery is defined by the same signals that showed the fault: throughput collapse onset at 07:42 (F8), lag rise to ~60k (F9/F30), and the two orders-3 error patterns (F10/F31).

recommended_actions.action: Add a poison-message / deserialization-failure dead-letter path with an alert that fires when a partition is blocked retrying a single offset, so a single unreadable record cannot silently halt an entire partition again.
recommended_actions.rationale: All 409 ERROR entries are retries of one offset on one partition (F10/F27/F28/F29); the existing tooling exposes no offset-skip or block-detection mechanism (F34), and the block persisted unnoticed from 07:42 to the 08:22 report.

recommended_actions.action: Introduce and enforce consumer-driven schema compatibility: versioned event contracts with backward compatibility, a schema registry / consumer contract test in CI, and required lockstep consumer updates when a producer bumps the event schema version.
recommended_actions.rationale: This is the first recorded schema-rename poisoning in the corpus (F16) and there is no precedent tying producer schema version bumps to consumer deserialization failures (F32 showed the exact schema change); a registry/contract gate prevents recurrence.

recommended_actions.action: Add per-partition lag/offset-progress and producer-side schema-version telemetry (plus the missing broker rebalance/reassignment/error metrics) so the causal hop — which producer emitted the blocking offset — can be proven directly next time.
recommended_actions.rationale: Metrics expose only aggregate consumer_lag; partition_lag, rebalance_count, partition_reassignment_count, broker_error_rate and offline_partitions all returned not_found (F26, F24), which is why the offset-to-producer link remains an assumption and could not be confirmed this time.

recommended_actions.action: Do not pursue broker-side partition reassignment remediation (e.g. restarting the consumer group as in HIST-112): the shared broker's other consumer is unaffected and under-replication is zero, so a reassignment theory is contradicted by evidence.
recommended_actions.rationale: notification-service lag is flat (~60) and throughput normal (132-167 req/s) on the same shared broker, its only WARN+ entry is unrelated NTP, and under_replicated_partitions is 0.0 for every bucket (F20/F21/F22/F23/F25).

data_gaps: No per-producer or per-partition telemetry exists to prove offset 8841207 was emitted by order-service: partition_lag returned not_found for settlement-service (only aggregate consumer_lag is exposed, F26), the kafka broker lacks rebalance/reassignment/error/offline metrics (F24), and order-service producer-metric queries were not completed (budget exhausted). The central causal hop therefore rests on deploy-content plus timing plus error-text match.

No consumer-group offset/commit view is exposed by any tool used, so it cannot be independently confirmed that the orders-3@8841207 record was produced after 07:40 rather than being an older record whose first parse attempt happened at 07:42.

Broker CPU and messages_in_per_s for the window were not queried (budget exhausted), leaving one remaining broker-health signal unchecked, though under_replicated_partitions=0.0 and both consumers' behavior indicate no broker-side disturbance.

Both log queries were truncated (409 and 52 total matches, 40 returned), so the complete absence of later (07:59-09:59) downstream/DB error signatures in the raw sample cannot be fully asserted, though the top_patterns aggregate lists only the two consumer-side patterns.

The producer-side schema version history for order-service and whether any other service emits to the orders topic could not be enumerated, so the assumption that orders-3's poison record is order-service v2 output is not directly verified at the source.

No historical precedent exists for a poison-message/deserialization stall or for a max.poll.records-type setting causing a stall, so neither today's signature nor the poll-config theory can be corroborated or refuted from precedent.
what_would_change_the_conclusion: Per-partition offset/commit telemetry or producer-side metrics showing that orders-3@8841207 was produced by a service other than order-service (e.g. payment-service), or that the blocking record predates the 07:40 deploy — this would move the conclusion toward H5 (non-order-service poison message).

Evidence that notification-service (the other consumer on the shared broker) also shows lag rise, throughput drop, rebalance, or the same deserialization/blocked symptom — this would revive H3 (broker-side event) and undercut the confinement argument.
Discovery of rebalance/session-timeout/poll-timeout log entries or non-zero under_replicated_partitions / partition-reassignment activity in the window — this would support H3 against H1.

Proof that the v2 poison record is readable by another consumer (or that offsets on orders-3 advanced while orders-0/orders-1 lag rose), which would indicate a settlement-service-specific consumer defect rather than a producer schema break.
Evidence that cfg-3004 did in fact cause fetch to stop (e.g. poll-timeout logs, a rebalance loop, or offset advance resuming on config revert before any schema fix) — this would point back to H2.
A ledger-db fault or connection-pool exhaustion signature timed to the onset, or a DB/post/5xx error in the truncated log region, which would revive H4 despite the currently flat DB counters.
A completed natural experiment: if rolling back order-service v2.16.0 (or skipping the poison offset) restores throughput and lag declines, H1 is confirmed; if not, H1 is falsified.
